name: Cantinarr
description: Cantinarr brings media requests and server management into one app. Household members browse and request movies, shows, books, and music, follow downloads, and get notified when content is ready. Admins manage Radarr, Sonarr, Chaptarr, Lidarr, and download clients, review approvals, and investigate stuck downloads from a phone or browser. Connect the services you use after setup. The web app runs in the same container, and the companion iPhone and Android apps connect to your server. Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Audiobookshelf, Tautulli, and Tracearr integrations are available. Import Doctor explains common download problems and offers fixes for an administrator to review. AI is optional. Connect a provider if you want an assistant for library questions and requests or an agent that investigates persistent download problems. Administrators choose what it may do. Cantinarr also offers MCP tools for authorized clients. The container serves its web app and API on port 8585. Service credentials stay server-side and are encrypted at rest. Sign-in uses connect links by default, with passwords and passkeys available when enabled.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Cantinarr's database and its generated encryption key. Instance API keys, download-client passwords, and AI credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted with that key, so back up this folder and keep it out of public shares.

paths.name: Media library (optional, read-only)
paths.description: Only needed if you want signed-in users to download completed files (ebooks, audiobooks, movies, episodes, tracks) from your library. Map the share holding that library here, then set Media roots below to /media. Leave blank to keep file downloads off.

ports.name: WebUI
ports.description: Port for the Cantinarr web app and API. The container always listens on 8585; change only the host side if something else already uses it.

variables.name: Push gateway URL
variables.description: Enables push notifications to the iOS and Android apps. Leave it set and the server enrolls itself on first start and stores its own key in the appdata volume, with no signup and no account. Clear the field to disable push entirely, or point it at your own gateway. The relay's former address, https://push.julian.codes, still works and is rewritten to the new one by current images.

variables.name: Arr webhook callback URL
variables.description: Origin your Radarr, Sonarr, and Chaptarr containers POST webhooks back to, so it has to be reachable from those containers. For example http://192.168.1.10:8585, or http://cantinarr:8585 on a shared Docker network. Leave blank to use whatever address you browse to. Set it explicitly behind a reverse proxy, because forwarded headers are deliberately ignored. This is not the address people reach Cantinarr at; set that in the app under Settings, External Address. Formerly named CANTINARR_PUBLIC_URL, which existing containers can keep using.

variables.name: Media roots
variables.description: Comma-separated container paths that completed-media downloads may serve from. Empty keeps downloads disabled. After mapping the read-only library above, set this to /media, then map each arr-reported path to a folder beneath it in that instance's settings. A bare / is refused.

variables.name: MCP OAuth issuer
variables.description: Only needed if you expose Cantinarr's Model Context Protocol endpoint to external AI clients through a reverse proxy. Set it to the canonical external HTTPS origin, for example https://cantinarr.example.com, and keep it stable, because changing it makes existing MCP clients reconnect.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User id the server runs as. On every start the container makes the appdata folder belong to this user, so its database and encryption key are owned by that user on the array (99 is Unraid's nobody). Leave blank to run as root, the previous behaviour.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group id to pair with PUID (100 is Unraid's users group). Ignored when PUID is blank.
